title: AI Scientists as Engines of Discovery: A Case for Development within Reformed Institutions
title_zh: 作为发现引擎的 AI 科学家：在改革后的制度中发展的论证
abstract_en: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems are beginning to assist, accelerate, and partially automate scientific discovery, performing tasks that span literature synthesis, code generation, data analysis, hypothesis proposal, and model criticism. We argue that this transition is qualitative rather than incremental, and that suitably designed multi-agent systems may evolve from passive computational tools into ``AI scientists'' that can expand the hypothesis-generating and verification capacity of science. Such systems must be developed and deployed within a scientific ecosystem fit for purpose: institutions must be redesigned for verification, accountability, interpretability, and dual-use safety. We sketch how multi-agent architectures, illustrated by the prototype framework \textit{Denario}, accelerate the discovery cycle and traverse model spaces beyond human reach; examine what this implies for authorship, peer review, and the enduring role of human scientists; and close with recommendations for governing AI as an epistemic actor rather than a mere instrument.
abstract_zh: 本文讨论具备自主性的人工智能（agentic AI）系统如何开始辅助、加速并部分自动化科学发现，覆盖文献综述、代码生成、数据分析、假设提出与模型批判等环节。作者认为，这一变化并非渐进式效率提升，而是科学实践的质变：设计良好的 multi-agent systems 有可能从被动计算工具演化为“AI scientists”，扩展科学中的假设生成与验证能力。与此同时，这类系统必须在适配其能力与风险的科研生态中开发和部署，相关机构需要围绕验证、问责、可解释性与 dual-use safety 重新设计。论文以原型框架 Denario 为例，说明 multi-agent architectures 如何加速发现循环，并探索超出人类可及范围的模型空间；随后讨论其对作者署名、同行评议以及人类科学家长期角色的影响；最后建议将 AI 作为一种“认知行动者”（epistemic actor）治理，而不仅仅视为工具。
key_points_zh: 论文主张 agentic AI 对科学发现的影响是质变而非简单增效，未来可能形成具备假设生成和验证能力的“AI scientists”。
multi-agent systems 被视为核心技术路径，可在文献综合、代码生成、数据分析、假设提出和模型批判之间形成自动化发现循环。
Denario 作为原型框架展示了 multi-agent architectures 如何加速科研流程，并探索超出人类直觉和计算能力范围的模型空间。
作者强调制度改革同等关键：科研机构需强化验证机制、问责体系、可解释性要求和 dual-use safety 治理。
论文重新审视 AI 参与科学后的作者署名、同行评议与人类科学家角色，建议将 AI 作为 epistemic actor 而非单纯工具来治理。

llm_assessment.comment: A broad position paper on AI scientists and institutions with some governance relevance, but limited concrete harness architecture or closed-loop implementation value.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 这是一篇关于AI科学家与制度的宽泛立场论文，具有一定治理相关性，但缺乏具体框架架构或闭环实现价值。
